title_checked: Decoding Time Series with LLMs: A Multi-Agent Framework for Cross-Domain Annotation
claim_summary: TESSA extracts numerical and textual features, selects salient features, and generates general then domain-specific temporal annotations.

modules.name: Multichannel temporal feature extraction
modules.scope_reason: Numerical time-series features and inter-variable correlations are shared inputs to annotation and downstream forecasting/imputation.

evidence.quote: We extract fea- tures from time series data through a structured process Mr. Formally, for each channel c ∈C, the set of time-series features Ft is denoted as: Ft = {f 1 t , · · · , f nt t } = Mr(X), (1) where Mr denotes the feature extraction frame- work applied to X, fi t is the i-th extracted feature of X, and nt is the number of extracted features.

modules.name: Domain annotation generation and review
modules.scope_reason: Term extraction and review optimize annotation relevance and alignment, not a generic forecast loop.

evidence.quote: To improve the quality of domain-specific annotations and ensure better alignment with general annotations, we introduce an annotation reviewer. This LLM, Mrev, reviews the generated annotations and extracted terms, pro- viding feedback ef to the extractor and annotator: ef = Mrev(prev(eg, et, {J i} nJ i=1)), (10) where prev is the prompt for reviewing annotations.

evaluation_summary: Annotation judged for clarity, comprehensiveness and domain relevance; Informer forecasting and imputation evaluate downstream utility.
corrections: Remove fabricated horizon/backtest contracts and direct forecasting-agent label. Annotation generation is a distinct task, not numerical data synthesis.

title_checked: TimeXL: Explainable Multi-Modal Time Series Prediction with LLM-in-the-Loop
claim_summary: TimeXL fuses prototype-based multimodal predictions with an LLM and iteratively refines textual context using training/validation feedback.

modules.name: Prototype explanation-conditioned predictive fusion
modules.scope_reason: Encoder and LLM outputs are fused for future discrete-label predictions.

evidence.quote: We compile the final prediction based on a fusion of both the multi-modal encoder Menc and prediction LLM Mpred. Specifically, we linearly combine the continuous prediction probabilities ˆyenc and discrete prediction ˆyLLM: ˆy = αˆyenc + (1 −α)ˆyLLM, where α ∈[0, 1] is the hyperparameter selected from validation data.

modules.name: Reflection-driven context refinement
modules.scope_reason: Feedback uses prediction ground truth to refine text and retrain the predictor; the loop is prediction-specific.

evidence.quote: Given the prediction ˆyLLM generated by the prediction agent Mpred, the reflection agent Mrefl aims to understand the reasoning behind the implicit prediction logic of Mpred.

evaluation_summary: Forecasts future price trends and health ratios as discrete labels; reports F1/AUROC on weather, finance and health tasks with 6:2:2 splits.
corrections: Do not describe ground-truth reflection as test-time access; Algorithm 1 separates training/validation and testing. Frozen language encoders/LLMs do not establish LLM-side training.

evidence.quote: To handle the multimodal inputs, ChatTS first separates the input time series arrays and the text.
